identity.title: DISCO: Mitigating Bias in Deep Learning with Conditional Distance Correlation

problem.claim: Dataset bias can cause deep learning models to rely on spurious correlations rather than task-relevant signals.

contributions.claim: Introduces the Standard Anti-Causal Model (SAM), a causal framework for characterizing bias mechanisms and defining a conditional-independence criterion for causal stability.
Proposes DISCO_m and sDISCO, efficient and scalable conditional distance-correlation estimators for independence regularization in gradient-based models.
Reports methods that outperform or match existing observed-bias mitigation approaches across six datasets, with fewer hyperparameters and support for multi-bias scenarios.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors state that the work unifies causal theory with practical deep-learning tools through SAM and conditional distance-correlation estimators.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that DISCO_m and sDISCO consistently outperform or are competitive with existing observed-bias mitigation approaches across six diverse datasets.
The authors report fewer hyperparameters and seamless scaling to multi-bias scenarios.

narrative_sequence.summary: Dataset bias may drive models toward spurious rather than task-relevant signals.
SAM is introduced to characterize bias mechanisms and formulate a conditional-independence criterion for causal stability.
DISCO_m and sDISCO operationalize the theory as scalable estimators for independence regularization.
Across six datasets, the methods are reported as outperforming or matching existing approaches while using fewer hyperparameters and handling multiple biases.

source_observation.claim: The abstract connects a causal framework and stability criterion to concrete regularizers and estimators, then reports comparisons on six datasets.

lessons.interpretation: A theory-to-method-to-evidence chain helps align the motivation, mechanism, and empirical claim.
lessons.application: State the formal criterion first, identify the model component that enforces it, and evaluate that component against the claimed failure mode.
lessons.exception: This structure may be unsuitable when the work is primarily descriptive or lacks a formal mechanism tied to the evaluation.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the six datasets, evaluation metrics, baseline methods, or the magnitude of performance differences.
The conditional-independence criterion, estimator formulations, multi-bias setup, and hyperparameter counts are not detailed.
No experimental conditions or evidence supporting the claimed causal stability are provided in the abstract.
